source_uncertainties: All nine contact sheets (three per lecture) were scanned before full frames were opened.

Slide defects corrected in reader text, each attributed: (1) L23 f0045 bracketed stress form omits rho on <u_i u_j> while the slide text names -rho<u_i u_j>; (2) L23 f0050 keeps n_i inside the volume integral after the divergence theorem; (3) L24 f0026 writes '<u_1^2> > 0' beside 'non-negative'; (4) L25 f0017 prints <u_3^2> in the (2,2) entry of the statistically 2D stress matrix; (5) L25 f0020 reads '<U_2> = 0 and <u_1u_2> = 0 are odd functions of x_2'; (6) L25 f0050 defines a_ij with <u_iu_i> in place of <u_iu_j>. The L25 slides write bar S_ij for the mean strain rate; the chapter writes <S_ij> and says so.

Slide text versus speech in L25 (frames f0030, f0039, f0053, f0057): slide text states Gamma_T and nu_T positive, the Boussinesq 1877 attribution, the Fourier/Fick and Newtonian analogies, 'basis for a lot of the earlier simplistic models', and the scaling of nu_T and Gamma_T with the flow scales (ratios increasing linearly with Re). Spoken only (not on any slide viewed, slide 26 of 27 is the last one shown before the credits): 'almost every turbulence model uses it', Pr_T approximately 1, 'data contradicts this hypothesis'.

Spoken statements corrected or qualified in reader text, each attributed: L24 ~895-1004 s 'isotropic part is the diagonal, anisotropic the off-diagonal' (a_ij has non-zero diagonal unless the normal stresses are equal; channel data show b_11 = 0.13 to 0.51); L25 ~364-470 s 'in irrotational flow the Reynolds stress has only an isotropic effect' (Corrsin and Kistler 1955 p. 15: the tensor need not be diagonal; only its divergence is a gradient); L25 604-622 s 'all you have is u1^2, u2^2, u3^2' in the channel (<u_1u_2> is odd in x_2 and carries 97 % of the stress at y/d = 0.1).
Lecture-stated value not checked against a source: turbulent Prandtl number nu_T/Gamma_T approximately 1 (L25 1674-1677 s). Attributed to the lecture in reader text.

Boussinesq (1877), Essai sur la theorie des eaux courantes, was not opened. The date, the 1872 meeting and the tensorial reading are taken from Schmitt (2007) and attributed to him; the attribution of the hypothesis to Boussinesq is also the lecture's (L25 1151-1156 s).

Lee and Moser (2015, J. Fluid Mech. 774) published paper not checked; the data files (header values, columns) and the 2014 arXiv preprint (pp. 3, 5) were checked. The running-case dimensional values (d = 2 cm, nu = 1.0e-6 m^2/s, rho = 1000 kg/m^3) are chosen inputs and are stated as such in reader text.

Schmitt (2007) reports the near-wall minimum of the total-stress alignment indicator at y+ = 10.5 +/- 0.5 for databases with friction Reynolds numbers 82 to 590 and a boundary layer; the same computation on the Lee-Moser files gives 0.238 at y+ = 13.8 (Re_tau 543), 0.229 at 14.2 (1000) and 0.209 at 14.8 (5186). The difference is reported, not explained.
Milani, Ling and Eaton (2020): arXiv preprint v2 cited; journal version not checked.

ASR spellings corrected: 'Bissonness', 'Bissoness' = Boussinesq; 'Corzine-Kitzler' = Corrsin-Kistler (slide: 'Corrsin Kistler equation'); 'round stresses', 'runner stresses', 'Ral stress', 'RSD' = Reynolds stresses; 'new' = nu; 'Ternikis and Nablus' = Tennekes and Lumley (not used in reader text); 'female' (L25 1749 s) = phi mean; 'phi components' (L25 1524 s) = five components; 'ionisotropic' = anisotropic; 'del x psi' = d/dx_i; 'impression' (L25 475 s) = pressure.
The lecture says the mean is averaged 'over a period of time' (L23 169-174 s); reader text uses the expectation and states the stationarity and ergodicity conditions for a time average.
Timestamps are section anchors from local speech-recognition segment times; they locate topic changes to within a few seconds.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.lecture_material: Constant-density incompressible setting of the module; the channel geometry with x_2 from the centreplane appears on the L25 symmetry slide.
sections.research_extension: Lee and Moser data files (Re_tau = 1000.512, U_b+ = 1/0.0500256 = 19.99, domain 8 pi d x 3 pi d) and arXiv preprint p. 3.
sections.teaching_construction: Formal model; the expectation as the averaging operator, with the time-average conditions; wall units; chosen dimensional values d = 2 cm, nu = 1e-6, rho = 1000 giving u_tau = 0.0500 m/s, U_b = 1.000 m/s, tau_w = 2.50 Pa.

sections.section: The Reynolds decomposition and the mean continuity equation
sections.lecture_material: Module introduction and Source slide (Pope 2000); Reynolds decomposition; <u> = 0; averaging continuity with commuting differentiation; mean and fluctuating fields each solenoidal.
sections.research_extension: None.
sections.teaching_construction: Averaging rules (9.2) stated with their conditions; <<U_i>u_j> = 0; channel consequence <U_2> = 0 from continuity and impermeable walls.

sections.section: Averaging the momentum equation: the Reynolds stresses appear
sections.lecture_material: Conservative substantial derivative; <U_iU_j> = <U_i><U_j> + <u_iu_j>; mean substantial derivative; Reynolds equations; the Reynolds-stress term as the crucial difference. Reynolds stresses zero in laminar flow (said at L23 1315 s, inside the next section's window; used here as the laminar check of (9.7)).
sections.research_extension: None.
sections.teaching_construction: Continuity step behind the conservative form; statement of what the derivation does not assume.

sections.section: The Poisson equation for the mean pressure
sections.lecture_material: Mean pressure satisfies a Poisson equation, by averaging or by taking the divergence of the Reynolds equations (slide f0036).
sections.research_extension: None.
sections.teaching_construction: Hinge: the fluctuation-gradient product equals the second derivative of <u_iu_j> because grad.u = 0; agreement of the two routes.

sections.section: The Reynolds stress as an apparent stress
sections.lecture_material: stress form with viscous, isotropic and apparent stresses; molecular versus fluctuating momentum transfer.
sections.research_extension: None.
sections.teaching_construction: Correction of the missing rho on slide f0045; separation of the covariance and stress sign conventions; where the molecular analogy holds and fails.

sections.section: The Reynolds stress as a mean momentum flux
sections.lecture_material: Control-volume rate of gain of momentum; mean of its j component; divergence theorem; Reynolds stress as mean momentum flux due to the fluctuating velocity.
sections.research_extension: Lee-Moser data: <u_1u_2>+ negative in the lower half, minimum -0.903 at y+ = 54.
sections.teaching_construction: Correction of n_i in the volume integral (f0050); heuristic for the negative sign of <u_1u_2>, labelled as heuristic.

sections.section: The Reynolds stress as a mean momentum flux (continued)
sections.lecture_material: Recap of the decomposition, the Reynolds equations, the strain-rate form of the viscous term and the momentum-flux interpretation.
sections.research_extension: As above.
sections.teaching_construction: As above.

sections.section: The running case: the Reynolds equations in a fully developed channel
sections.lecture_material: None (the channel and its statistical one-dimensionality appear in L25 and in chapter 8).
sections.research_extension: Lee-Moser data: max |dU+/dy+ - <uv>+ - (1 - y/d)| = 3.9e-4 over 256 points; P column satisfies P+ + <vv>+ = 0 to 2e-15 (the file's convention for the mean pressure, derived from (9.12), not an independent check; preprint p. 3); crossover y+ ~ 11; Reynolds share 97.3 % at y/d = 0.1; preprint p. 5 (total-stress linearity as stationarity test).
sections.teaching_construction:
Reduction (9.11)-(9.13);

+ rho = p_w(x_1); laminar comparison U_b+ = Re_tau/3 = 333.5 against 19.99 (factor 16.7); Figure 9.1.

sections.section: The closure problem: four equations and ten unknowns
sections.lecture_material: Four independent equations (three Reynolds plus continuity or Poisson, not both); more than four unknowns; six independent Reynolds stresses by symmetry; normal and shear stresses; 'unsolved problem' framing.
sections.research_extension: None.
sections.teaching_construction: Explicit count 4 against 10; channel count 1 against 2; moment hierarchy via third moments (Exercise 1); forward pointers to chapters 16 and 18 by manifest title.

sections.section: Properties of the Reynolds-stress tensor
sections.lecture_material: k as half the trace; mean kinetic energy per unit mass of the fluctuations; principal axes; non-negative eigenvalues; symmetric positive semi-definite.
sections.research_extension: Lee-Moser data: rho_12 = -0.41 at y/d = 0.1, between -0.396 and -0.417 for 0.05 <= y/d <= 0.5.
sections.teaching_construction: Proof of positive semi-definiteness by the quadratic form; Cauchy-Schwarz consequence; realizability; correction of '> 0' on f0026.

sections.section: Isotropic and anisotropic parts
sections.lecture_material: Isotropic stress 2/3 k delta_ij; a_ij; b_ij; <u_iu_j> = 2/3 k delta_ij + a_ij = 2k(delta_ij/3 + b_ij).
sections.research_extension: Lee-Moser data: b diagonal at y+ = 1, y/d = 0.1 and near the centreplane; |b_12| <= 0.135; b_22 = -0.333 at the wall; max b_11 = 0.512 at y+ = 7.8.
sections.teaching_construction: Correction of 'diagonal = isotropic'; derivation of the bounds -1/3 <= b_aa <= 2/3, |b_ab| <= 1/2 and of the eigenvalue range.

sections.section: Only the anisotropic part transports momentum: the modified mean pressure
sections.lecture_material:
Substitution of the decomposition into the pressure and Reynolds-stress terms; Kronecker delta switches the index; modified mean pressure =

+ 2/3 rho k; only a_ij effective in transporting momentum.
sections.research_extension: None.
sections.teaching_construction:
Mechanism: a gradient force is absorbed by the pressure of incompressible flow; boundaries (pressure boundary conditions, k needed to recover

); channel value p_m - p_w = -2 rho k b_22, 2.9 Pa at y/d = 0.1.

sections.section: Only the anisotropic part transports momentum (recap)
sections.lecture_material: Recap of the isotropic part absorbed into the pressure.
sections.research_extension: As above.
sections.teaching_construction: As above.

sections.section: Irrotational fluctuations: the Corrsin-Kistler result
sections.lecture_material: Irrotational flow: zero vorticity; derivation of d<u_iu_j>/dx_i = dk/dx_j (Corrsin Kistler equation, slide f0004); Reynolds stress acts like an isotropic stress; turbulence is rotational.
sections.research_extension: Corrsin and Kistler 1955, NACA Report 1244, p. 15 (PDF p. 18), eqs. (23)-(25) and the following sentences: no net apparent shear forces; the tensor need not have only diagonal terms.
sections.teaching_construction: Index steps of the derivation; condition on a_ij compatible with (9.21); qualification of the lecture's 'only isotropic effect'.

sections.section: Reflection symmetries of the Reynolds stresses
sections.lecture_material: Statistically 2D flow invariant under x_3 reflection: <U_3> = <u_1u_3> = <u_2u_3> = 0; channel symmetric about x_2 = 0.
sections.research_extension: Lee-Moser data: max |<u_1u_3>+| = 4.9e-3, |<u_2u_3>+| = 4.7e-4 against 0.903; max |W+| = 8.6e-3 (3.8e-4 of the centreline velocity); header calls them quality indicators.
sections.teaching_construction: Derivation from the PDF; correction of the (2,2) slide entry and of the conclusion that only normal stresses remain; <U_2> = 0 attributed to continuity.

sections.section: The mean scalar equation and the scalar flux
sections.lecture_material: Scalar decomposition; averaged scalar equation; turbulent scalar flux; scalar closure problem; temperature as an example.
sections.research_extension: None.
sections.teaching_construction: Unit of the flux; count of new unknowns.

sections.section: The gradient-diffusion hypothesis
sections.lecture_material: Hypothesis <u phi'> = -Gamma_T grad<phi>; effective diffusivity; flow property not fluid property; used by almost every turbulence model (lecture's judgement).
sections.research_extension: Milani, Ling, Eaton 2020 (arXiv v2): p. 1 two types of counter-gradient transport in an inclined jet in crossflow and a stable tensor diffusivity; p. 3 definition and earlier reports; pp. 8-9 near-wall type with both v'c' and dc/dy positive and pressure-scalar correlation.
sections.teaching_construction: Separation of the alignment and sign claims; ill-posedness of Gamma_eff < 0 (growth rate |Gamma_eff| kappa^2); link to chapter 4's K.

sections.section: The turbulent-viscosity hypothesis
sections.lecture_material: Boussinesq 1877 (lecture's attribution); analogy with the Newtonian stress; deviatoric Reynolds stress proportional to the mean strain rate; nu_eff; modified pressure; five components related through nu_T.
sections.research_extension: Schmitt 2007 (HAL preprint pp. 3-4): 1877 publication reporting an 1872 Academy meeting; Reynolds 1895; tensorial form of Boussinesq's expressions.
sections.teaching_construction: Why the deviatoric part is required (trace argument); alignment of principal axes; reduction of unknowns to nu_T and Gamma_T.

sections.section: Shear-flow forms, scaling, and what the hypothesis leaves open
sections.lecture_material: Boundary-layer forms with opposite signs; specifying nu_T and Gamma_T solves the closure; nu_T and Gamma_T scale with the flow and grow linearly with Re away from walls; Pr_T approximately 1; data contradict the hypothesis but it is the simplest closure.
sections.teaching_construction: Evaluation of nu_T from the DNS; quantitative test of the Re-scaling statement; link to (4.13).

sections.section: Testing the turbulent-viscosity hypothesis on the channel
sections.lecture_material: None (the lecture states only that data contradict the hypothesis).
sections.research_extension: Schmitt 2007: indicator and 0.86 threshold (p. 6), databases (pp. 6-7), total-stress alignment poor for 3 < y+ < 70 with minimum at y+ = 10.5 +/- 0.5 (p. 8), annular-pipe point with S = 0 and R non-zero (p. 8), 'almost never verified' (p. 1), mean fields versus second moments (p. 10). Lee-Moser data: b_11 0.13-0.51, b_22 -0.33 to -0.06; gamma_aS turbulent 0.013 to at most 0.59; total 0.996 at y+ 1, below 0.86 beyond y+ 2.9, near-wall minimum 0.23 at y+ 14, 0.018 near the centreplane. Lee-Moser data at Re_tau 543 and 5186: minimum of gamma_aS with viscous stress at y+ = 13.8 (0.238) and 14.8 (0.209); running case max <u_1^2>+ = 8.10 at y+ = 15.2, one grid point from the minimum.
sections.teaching_construction: TVH prediction of isotropic normal stresses in simple shear; gamma_aS for the channel reduces to sqrt(2)|<uv>|/|a|; Figure 9.2.

sections.section: Executable check: the channel data against the equations and the hypothesis
sections.lecture_material: Matrices of practice problem L59-P8.
sections.research_extension: Nine rows of the Lee-Moser Re_tau = 1000 files and two header values.
sections.teaching_construction: NumPy program: realizability by eigenvalues, k, a_ij, b_ij, three assertions per row (b eigenvalues in [-1/3, 2/3], zero trace, total stress = 1 - y/d within 2e-3), nu_T, gamma_aS with and without viscous stress, laminar comparison, running-case units, L59-P8 rejection; failure test flipping one <uv> sign.

sections.research_extension: Schmitt 2007; Milani et al. 2020; Corrsin and Kistler 1955.
sections.teaching_construction: Classification of exact results, constraints and models; a priori versus a posteriori testing.

references.title: Corrsin and Kistler 1955, Free-stream boundaries of turbulent flows (NACA Report 1244)
references.supports: Eq. (24): for irrotational fluctuations d(u_iu_j)/dx_j = (1/2) d(q^2)/dx_i; eq. (25) with P + (rho/2) q^2; 'irrotational fluctuations give no net apparent shear forces on a fluid element'; 'This does not necessarily mean, however, that the Reynolds shear force on a plane is zero or that the Reynolds stress tensor -rho u_iu_k has only leading diagonal terms.'
references.page_checked: report p. 15 (PDF p. 18), page image rendered and read

references.title: Schmitt 2007, About Boussinesq's turbulent viscosity hypothesis: historical remarks and a direct evaluation of its validity (C. R. Mecanique 335, 617-627; HAL hal-00264386)
references.supports: p. 1: hypothesis 'almost never verified'; p. 3: 1877 publication is a report of an 1872 Academy meeting, Reynolds 1895; p. 4: Boussinesq's stresses as tensorial closure, eq. (5); p. 5: R = -2 nu_T S, eq. (8); p. 6: indicator rho_RS = |R:S|/(|R||S|), 0.86 for angles below pi/6, databases; p. 7: normal stresses unequal so the hypothesis cannot hold, eq. (11), total stress aligned very close to the wall; p. 8: alignment bad for 3 < y+ < 70, minimum at y+ = 10.5 +/- 0.5, annular pipe point with S = 0 and R non-zero; p. 10: models predict mean fields of simple flows, second moments not satisfactory.
references.page_checked: HAL preprint pp. 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 (PDF pp. 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11); journal pagination 617-627 not checked

references.title: Milani, Ling and Eaton 2020, Turbulent scalar flux in inclined jets in crossflow: counter gradient transport and deep learning modelling (arXiv:2001.04600v2)
references.supports: p. 1: highly resolved LES at velocity ratios 1 and 2; two types of counter-gradient transport (windward shear layer, cross-gradient; near wall after injection, non-local); matrix diffusivity ensured stable. p. 3: counter-gradient = a flux component with the same sign as the gradient component, 'directly contradicts' the GDH with positive diffusivity; earlier reports. pp. 8-9: Type 2, both v'c' and dc/dy positive; budget points to non-local effects, chiefly fluctuating pressure.
references.page_checked: arXiv preprint pp. 1, 3, 8, 9 (same as PDF pages); journal version not checked
